Agency.question: Who actually initiates action?
Agency.indicator: override cost; share of actions initiated by system vs user
Agency.reason: user initiates sessions, but assistant pre-populates defaults, suggested prompts, and tool uses; override is possible but requires user awareness

Value.question_v2: For declared-objective architectures: does the operational objective diverge from the declared? For undeclared architectures, this row reduces to Authority + Contestability.
Value.indicator: declared-operational gap; for undeclared architectures: not applicable
Value.reason: declared objective is 'helpful and safe'; observed behavior optimizes for a narrower operationalization of safety that is not in the declared philosophy — this is the dark-ontology pattern of §6
Value.value_load_prediction: yes (consistent with refined Pass IV prediction)

Authority.question: Who can make irreversible decisions?
Authority.reason: OpenAI holds unilateral, irreversible rights to terminate accounts and access; user appeal channel exists but is opaque

Memory.question: What persists, and who owns it?
Memory.reason: export tool exists and works; retention persists indefinitely unless deleted; third-party control is high (OpenAI controls storage, indexing, and derived embeddings)

Exit.question: Can participants meaningfully leave?
evidence: no API-level portability of fine-tuned behavior
Exit.reason: export gives raw transcripts, not the computational structure (system prompt behavior, fine-tuned weights, custom instructions, learned preferences); architectural barrier is high for any sustained user

Contestability.question: Can rules and decisions be challenged?
evidence: no public mechanism for policy change
Contestability.indicator: existence and cost of a procedure that has changed a rule
Contestability.reason: no documented case where user appeal changed a usage policy; rule changes are announced, not negotiated

Materiality.question: Who owns and can block the infrastructure?
Materiality.reason: OpenAI is sole provider of canonical weights, inference compute, and API access; a single corporate veto covers the system

Labor.question: Who does the hidden work?
Labor.reason: labor is acknowledged in system cards but not visible per-task to users; compensation and working conditions have been reported as variable

Legitimacy.question: Why may it constrain alternatives?
Legitimacy.reason: justification appeals to safety and public benefit; whether the alternatives actually available to users meet the threshold is unexamined

Reconstructability.question: Can a different version be built?
evidence: open-weight alternatives exist (Llama, Mistral) but at lower capability
Reconstructability.reason: alternative cost is falling but the canonical GPT-4-class system is not reconstructible by an individual or small institution at this date

agency_profile.reversibility: Mixed (low for in-chat actions; high for tool-mediated actions)
agency_profile.verdict: Effective agency is low even where formal agency is preserved; matches §13 prediction
